memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But a prophet who presumes to speak in my name anything I have not commanded, or a prophet who speaks in the name of other gods, is to be put to death. You may say to yourselves, "How can we know when a message has not been spoken by the Lord?" - Deut 18:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God knew that alongside true prophets, false ones would arise, people who spoke their own ideas in God's name, or who spoke in the name of false gods. Under Israel's law, this was a capital offence, because leading people astray with lies about God did enormous spiritual damage. Then God anticipates the people's honest question, "How can we know when a message has not been spoken by the Lord?"

This is a real and important question. Not everyone who claims to speak for God actually does. God cared that His people would not be deceived, so He did not leave them defenceless. He was about to give them a clear test to discern truth from falsehood.

We face the same challenge today. Many voices claim to speak for God, and not all of them are true. The New Testament urges us to test the spirits, because many false prophets have gone out into the world (1 John 4:1). How do we test them? By measuring their message against God's revealed Word, and by looking to Christ, who is the truth. We are not left defenceless either; we have the Scriptures and the Spirit to help us discern. Are you careful to test the many voices you hear against the sure truth of God's Word?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do you test the voices claiming to speak for God?
2. Do you measure teaching against Scripture?
3. Where do you need more discernment right now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me discernment to test every voice against Your Word. Guard me from deception and root me in Your truth. Amen.
